findings.description: The distinction between a changed request and changed sources is a stated requirement and a proof obligation, but has no typed spelling in the closed vocabulary. C25 requires that a changed request 'may reject continuation as query-mismatched, not be mislabeled source change'; bp-0007's proof builds 'stale/malformed/query-mismatched continuation cases' and its note states 'Query mismatch remains distinct from source change'; query-contract.md states 'changing a page size or available output columns is not a source change'. Yet C10 is unchanged and collapses both causes into one outcome ('changed source view or options refuse StaleCursor'), C14's closed code list offers only StaleCursor with ViewScopeMismatch already assigned to C23's execute_view widening refusal, C21's RecoveryAction offers only StartFreshQuery, C14's fixed explanation is 'stale cursor says start a fresh query', and C21 forbids free-form diagnostic detail strings. Both digests are opaque to callers, so a caller who changed only --limit and a caller whose sources moved receive an identical typed answer. This is not a contradiction because StaleCursor is a cause-neutral name and nothing in the guide is false as written; it is an unimplementable proof obligation, since a lane writing bp-0007's query-mismatched case has nothing contract-visible to assert on and would have to invent either a code or a forbidden detail string. Minimal fix: add one enumerated distinction to the wave0 declarations, either a distinct QueryFailureCode such as RequestMismatch or a closed reason discriminant on StaleCursor, and align C10's single-outcome sentence. Belongs in tk-0001 before team/baseline.dd.json is sealed, because C21's own rule returns a changed shared failure enum to tk-0001 and invalidates dependent proof.
